# `unflushed-writer`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a buffered `std.Io` file or stream writer that is written but not
flushed on every path: never flushed, flushed only in a branch, or left behind
by an early `return`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A buffered `std.Io` writer keeps written bytes in its buffer until `flush` (or
the file writer's `end`) hands them to the file or stream. Nothing flushes on
scope exit, so output that never fills the buffer, or the tail of output that
did, is silently dropped: a generator that prints nothing, or a file that is
cut short.

## When it fires

The rule tracks local writers created by `file.writer(io, &buffer)`,
`writerStreaming`, or `File.Writer.init`, `initStreaming` and `initDetect`,
together with aliases such as `const stdout = &stdout_writer.interface`. It
reports a writer that is written to (`print`, `writeAll`, `writeByte` and the
other writing methods) but that its scope never flushes, ends or seeks.

A flush counts only on the paths that run it. When the writer is flushed but a
write has a path to the end of the scope that skips every flush, for example a
flush inside an `if` or a write after the last flush, the writer is reported as
flushed on only some paths, with the write as a related location. A plain
`return` (or `orelse return`) reached after a write with no flush in between is
reported at the `return`. Error returns, `return error.X` and returns inside a
`catch` or `else |err|` handler, are left alone, and a loop body is assumed to
run. An `if` that ends in a plain `else`, or a `switch`, flushes when every
branch does (a prong that is `unreachable` or `@panic(...)` never finishes, so
it needs none). A flush in a `defer` covers every path.

Returning or storing the writer, for example in a struct field such as
`std.zig.Server.out`, hands the flush to its new owner. Passing it to a
function follows that function: a helper that flushes or keeps its parameter
counts as a flush, and one that only writes counts as a write. Helpers in the
same file are read directly; project analysis reads helpers in other files.
A callee neither can read, such as a standard-library function, keeps the
writer quiet. Writers with an empty buffer (`&.{}`) write straight through and
are not reported.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void {
    var buffer: [256]u8 = undefined;
    var stdout_writer = std.Io.File.stdout().writer(init.io, &buffer);
    const stdout = &stdout_writer.interface;
    try stdout.print("hello\n", .{});
}
```
